#773. Spain test will reveal if Tuchel and England have learned World Cup lessons

England head coach Thomas Tuchel during the World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina in Atlanta

England's proof of progress and the lessons learned by head coach Thomas Tuchel since the disappointment of World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina will be put to the sternest test when they face holders Spain in Madrid.

Spain present the toughest assignment England could face, with the world champions' unbeaten run â in which they claimed the sport's biggest prize by beating Argentina in New Jersey in the summer â now stretching to 43 games.

Luis de la Fuente's side last lost - to Colombia - in March 2024, winning 34 games and drawing nine in the intervening period, during which they also became European champions, beating England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.

Little wonder, then, that England captain and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane describes Sunday night's visit to the Metropolitano Stadium as: "The perfect opportunity to try and prove ourselves."

Tuchel, who revealed Leeds United's James Trafford will get another opportunity in goal as he continues to alternate with Jordan Pickford, clearly feels the same as he added: "This will be proof of concept on the highest level. It's the biggest test in world football. Spain are unbelievable on an incredible run.

"Spain won the last big titles. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are in a good moment to push our limits. We are up for something spectacular."

It was a message echoed here in Madrid by England midfielder Declan Rice, who said: "It's a massive game.

"I don't think you can get much bigger than a Champions League final with Arsenal or a World Cup semi-final against Argentina, which I've played in, but when you are playing against the world champions in Spain there is no greater incentive.

"It's the sort of game that brings out the best in us. We want to play against the best teams and the best players. It will show where we are as a group. We're going to see where England are at."

Spain are particularly formidable on home soil, unbeaten in 20 games - winning 15 and drawing five - since a 2-1 defeat by Switzerland in September 2022.

England's most recent win in Spain was a 3-2 triumph in a Nations League encounter in Sevilla in October 2018, their first away victory against them for 31 years.

Yet England came closer than most to piercing Spain's air of invincibility, even though they lost 3-2 at Wembley in September, when a rare Kane blemish from the penalty spot prevented them taking a potentially decisive 3-1 lead.

Spain subsequently punished England and Kane, who will be hoping for better fortunes when the countries meet again in the latest Nations League encounter.

England arrived in Madrid on Saturday evening having reeled off four successive victories since that Wembley loss, the latest of which was a 2-1 win against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

Spain will present an altogether different opposition, but also a barometer of whether England have moved forward since the World Cup, when Tuchel was heavily criticised for what was perceived to be a negative approach in the 2-1 loss to Argentina in Atlanta, especially after Anthony Gordon put England ahead.

'The decisions Tuchel made cost England' - analysis

Former England defender Matthew Upson, who will be in Madrid for BBC Radio 5 Live, told BBC Sport: "Harry Kane saying this is the perfect opportunity for England to prove themselves is a great way to build this challenge up.

"I wouldn't expect anything less from him considering where he is at now, where his belief level is and what he wants to achieve.

"Harry is achieving incredible personal accolades like the Ballon d'Or, but he won't rest there. He will want a team honour with England, and if you play against the best in the world there is no better barometer of where you're at as a group.

"It's going to be a very interesting test. It's fair to say we didn't see England at full flow against Croatia, so now we will see if they adjust, improve and produce something of their best, which they will have to do if you are going to get any sort of result against Spain in Spain.

"If England get a point, or even better a win, against Spain with their record, at home and away, we will come away thinking they are at a high level.

"If you get a result, you will have had to play really well because you won't do that with anything else.

"By that, I don't mean a blistering game. I just mean doing things well and showing the level you are at."

In the aftermath of that World Cup loss to Argentina, the post-tournament process embarked upon by the Football Asssociation included canvassing the opinions of the whole squad, where it emerged it took place at a "full and frank" meeting with Tuchel at the start of the September international break.

Kane and Jude Bellingham were understood to have given forthright views, where the approach in the devastating loss to Argentina was a key theme.

There is now believed to be a feeling in the squad that Tuchel has taken on the lessons of Atlanta and is focusing on a more positive approach.

Spain won Euro 2024 and this year's World Cup

Upson said: "England are still a bit of a work in progress. We have two or maybe three players who are playing some of the best football across Europe and the world at the moment. I am thinking of Kane, Bellingham and, at times, Anthony Gordon.

"The key is utilising that, then getting the rest of the team to a place where it can support that and deliver its own world-class support. This is the challenge for Thomas Tuchel."

"England are adopting a more positive approach, but look a little vulnerable defensively, which is maybe the compromise.

"Yes, England could have been 3-1 up against Spain had Harry Kane scored his penalty, but don't forget we could easily have been 3-0 down before we scored."

The intense environment of facing the World Cup holders on their own turf will also be a forensic examination of England's mental progress as well as footballing prowess.

Upson said: "The biggest thing to fix after the World Cup was player reaction and player belief when we're in certain situations, especially if we go ahead and all of a sudden the game is difficult, as it was against Argentina. What is our mindset going to be?

"Since then England have tried to play much more freely, openly and confidently. That's how I see it. That's how we played when we won 7-0 in Croatia. We were free, open, positive. Belief was through the roof.

"This is why this test against Spain is great because you will get tested to the maximum there. If England go ahead, let's see how they do and what they do. If they go behind, let's see what we do.

"Against Spain at Wembley, I saw a reaction at half-time from England, which was fantastic. We should have gone 3-1 up with Harry's penalty, and in that 15 minutes after half-time we were super positive, aggressive in our decision-making.

"This was another ideal situation to test that. They came through that really positively. It would be great if we get another test like that on Sunday.

"It it all plays into what Harry Kane said. This is something which will test people. It's a really significant game for England on a lot of levels."

#772. Taylor Frankie Paul's Ex Dakota Mortensen Suing Hulu for Defamation

Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Dakota Mortensen, who has appeared on the Hulu reality show alongside his ex Taylor Frankie Paul, has filed a lawsuit against the network, alleging staged events.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives alum—who has appeared on the Hulu reality series with his now-ex Taylor Frankie Paul—has filed a lawsuit against the network, as well as Jeff Jenkins Productions and Ludwig Productions, according to court documents obtained by multiple outlets Nov. 13.

In his suit, the 33-year-old alleged that seasons three, four, and five of the series presented him "to millions of viewers as a domestic abuser," per court documents obtained by local outlet ABC4 Utah, "as a man who retaliated against the mother of his child by reporting her to Child Protective Services, and as a serial adulterer.”

Earlier this year, a legal battle between Mortensen and Paul—who share a 2-year-old son—began after he filed to request a protective order against on her on the same day that TMZ published a video of a 2023 physical altercation featuring the former couple.

In April, Paul—who is also mom to two kids with ex-husband Tate Paul—then requested her own temporary restraining order, alleging Mortensen had a "pattern of abusive conduct and coercive control" throughout their on-again, off-again romance.

Later that month, per Today, a judge granted mutual protective orders.

Mortensen also alleges in his lawsuit against the network that producers created storylines "assembled from staged events and from the deliberate deletion of footage that contradicted the storyline, and published after the producers had been informed by Mortensen and by others, that the allegations were false."

More specifically, Mortensen alleges cameras captured Paul striking Mortensen with a pizza box while filming season five, per ABC 4 Utah, and demanded that the footage be included in the episodes that aired, but that it was excluded from the final cut.

E! News has reached out to Paul’s reps for comment about the alleged incident.

“The knowingly false portrayal of Mortensen as the abuser in the relationship continued uninterrupted," the suit states, "while the only footage of physical aggression between the two, aggression by Paul against Mortensen, was intentionally withheld from viewers to promote a false narrative."

Mortensen is asking for compensatory damages, ABC 4 Utah reports, as well as other damages. E! News has reached out to Hulu and Mortensen's attorney for comment and has not yet heard back.

In mid-April, Paul was granted supervised visitation with her and Mortensen's son and one week later, the Salt Lake County District Attorney’s Office announced in a news release it would not be filing charges against her after completing two separate investigations led by the Draper Police Department and West Jordan Police Department.

For his part, Mortensen previously described the situation between the two as “deeply upsetting.”

“I am focusing on our son and his safety,” he told E! News in a statement in March, “and hope that Taylor will do the same.”

For a closer look at the timeline of the allegations made between Paul and Mortensen, keep reading…

Feb. 17, 2023: Taylor Frankie Paul Arrested Following Confrontation With Dakota Mortensen

After rising to fame with #MomTok, Taylor Frankie Paul was arrested in Utah on Feb. 17, 2023 stemming from an incident with then boyfriend Dakota Mortensen. She was accused of throwing metal chairs and a wooden playset at him while one of her two children—who she shares with ex-husband Tate Paul—was in the room, per an affidavit obtained by ABC 4 Utah.

Paul was charged with one count of felony aggravated assault, two counts of felony domestic violence in the presence of a child causing injury, one count of misdemeanor child abuse and one count of misdemeanor criminal mischief, according to court documents released by the District Attorney for Salt Lake County and obtained by E! News at the time.

A Herriman Police Department officer who responded to the incident said that when he arrived, Mortensen "reported he was in an argument with his girlfriend,” according to a written declaration in the court documents. The officer further stated that "during the argument, Mortensen attempted to leave the residence, however [Paul] began hitting him."

August 2023: Taylor Frankie Paul Pleads Guilty to Aggravated Assault

Paul pleaded guilty to a third-degree felony count of aggravated assault in August 2023, according to court documents obtained by the Salt Lake Tribune, while four other charges were dismissed with prejudice.

Her plea was held in abeyance for three years, at which time the charge would be entered as a Class A misdemeanor as long as Paul abided by the terms of her plea agreement, per the documents.

According to her plea deal, Paul was to obtain both a substance abuse evaluation and a domestic violence evaluation and complete any recommended treatment over a three-year period—as well as not violate any major laws.

March 19, 2024: Taylor Frankie Paul and Dakota Mortensen Welcome Son

Paul and Mortensen's son was born a week early, with Paul posting a photo from the hospital to Instagram on April 4, 2024 and writing, “We’ve had the best two weeks with him. We all love you so much, thank you for blending our family.”

September 2024: Taylor Frankie Paul Speaks Out About 2023 Arrest

Paul admitted in an interview with E! News that the altercation with Mortensen was their “rock bottom for sure.”

"He stood by me with that because he knew everything going on behind closed doors,” she said. “That was a horrible night and I'm full of regret. Dakota has been at rock bottom himself, so he could totally relate. He was like, 'I want to help you out of this.'"

As for the confrontation itself, she later said the incident had been building up.

“I had an ectopic [pregnancy] a few months prior, and then I had a chemical pregnancy,” she shared on the Viall Files podcast in September 2024. “I don't want to blame hormones, but I will put that into account. Like, I am pretty whack.”

Paul added that the events had left her feeling lost and angry, saying, "I was feeling so low I went and drank that night. And Dakota picks me up and he’s angry that I drank."

"I remember throwing things, and I don't know my daughters on the couch. We had babysitters there, so I think they’re upstairs sleeping," she said, alleging that Mortensen tried to tell her that her then 5-year-old daughter was present, but "I'm like so gone I don’t care, and I throw another chair."

Sept. 6, 2024: Secret Lives of Mormon Wives Premieres

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives debuted on Hulu in September 2024, with the first episode of season one featuring Paul's 2023 arrest.

May 18, 2025: Taylor Frankie Paul Confirms Dakota Mortensen Breakup After On-Again, Off-Again Relationship

Paul confirmed their split in May 2025 after it was revealed on the season two premiere of SLOMW that Mortensen had cheated on her shortly after they had welcomed their son, writing on TikTok, "Dakota isn’t mine anymore, wish him the best.”

"Dakota and I were living together and in bliss with our new baby, and I was even considering engagement,” she said on the premiere episode. “And then I learned that he was lying this entire time.”

During a season four episode of SLOMW, Mortensen admitted to cheating with their friend Shinia Powell, telling Taylor during a FaceTime call, “Was it dumb of me? Yes. Could I have picked someone else? Yes. Who it was matters, and that's where I think I went wrong. I picked somebody that was obviously going to come with problems, and that was very s--tty of me to do."

Sept. 10, 2025: Taylor Frankie Paul Is Cast as The Bachelorette for Season 22

In a surprising turn of events, Paul was cast as the leading lady for season 22 of The Bachelorette, confirming the news during an appearance on Call Her Daddy in September 2025. The decision marked a notable departure for the franchise, as it usually casts suitors from previous seasons of The Bachelor in the position.

But for Paul, it was a welcome change, saying in a teaser for the season, “I do believe I was gifted this for another chapter in my life.”

“I’ve been criticized, I’ve been judged and I’ve been rejected,” Paul continued, “but anyone that takes the time to know me will see that I’m actually a genuine person and I mean well and a person that deserves another chance at love.”

Fall 2025: Taylor Frankie Paul and Dakota Mortensen FaceTime Before Filming Begins on The Bachelorette

Shortly before Paul began filming season 22 of The Bachelorette, she and Mortensen shared an emotional conversation seen during a season four episode of SLOMW, during which he apologized for having a relationship with Shinia, saying it was "very s--tty of me to do."

He added that he and Paul had both done “a lot of things” to “hurt each other,” but believed that overall the two still loved each other.

The pair agreed their relationship was “toxic,” with Paul saying that being on The Bachelorette "will be one the best things for us, regardless of what happens. This would be the best break and breakoff of our cycle. You could do a lot of healing."

But Mortensen made it clear he was still interested in a relationship, telling Paul, “I'm happy for you. I want you to be happy. That's what I'm saying, if you find someone, like, great. But all I'm gonna say—save a rose for me, 'kay?"

February 2026: Taylor Frankie Paul and Dakota Mortensen's Domestic Assault Investigation Opened

Filming for season five of Secret Lives of Mormon Wives was put on hold after an alleged confrontation between Paul and Mortensen in February 2026.

A spokesperson for the Draper City Police Department confirmed to People on March 16 that there was an open "domestic assault investigation" regarding Paul and Mortensen—telling the outlet that "allegations have been made in both directions.” The spokesperson explained "contact was made with involved parties on [Feb] 24th and 25th,” but declined to share more information due to the ongoing investigation.

As a source shared with E! News, "Taylor owns her mistakes, all she wants to do is protect her son, Ever, from stories in the press or anything negative about his father and wants him to think well of his father."

March 19, 2026: Footage From Taylor Frankie Paul and Dakota Mortensen’s 2023 Confrontation Surfaces

Following news of Paul and Mortensen's 2026 dispute, video footage from their physical altercation in 2023 was released by TMZ.

In the video, Mortensen can be seen recording the fight on his phone as Paul yells at him and attempts to strike him, at one point putting him in a headlock.

"Look," Mortensen can be heard saying, "this is called physical abuse."

He could also be heard telling her that her daughter was present as Paul began throwing metal barstools at him. During the altercation, Paul accused Mortensen of pushing her to the floor before he started recording, while he alleged, "You did this," and asked her to help her then-5-year-old. Later, Paul could be heard yelling, "Get away from my daughter."

The responding police officer’s written declaration obtained by E! News in 2023 confirmed the child was hit by one of the stools.

After the video was published, a spokesperson for Paul told E! News in a statement that the video was part of "a destructive campaign to harm" her, saying it "conveniently omits context" and was meant to "distract" from Mortensen's actions. As for the real estate agent, he denied her claims as "baseless."

March 19, 2026: ABC Cancels Taylor Frankie Paul’s Season of The Bachelorette

After video of the 2023 altercation between Paul and Mortensen surfaced, ABC confirmed that it would be cancelling season 22 of The Bachelorette, with a spokesperson for Disney Entertainment saying in a statement to E! News, “We have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of The Bachelorette at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family.”

March 19, 2026: Taylor Frankie Paul Speaks Out on Bachelorette Cancelation

Following ABC’s decision, Paul broke her silence about the situation.

"Taylor is very grateful for ABC’s support as she prioritizes her family’s safety and security," her rep told E! News. "After years of silently suffering extensive mental and physical abuse as well as threats of retaliation, Taylor is finally gaining the strength to face her accuser and taking steps to ensure that she and her children are protected from any further harm."

The statement continued, "There are too many women who are suffering in silence as they survive aggressive, jealous ex-partners who refuse to let them move on with their lives."

Her rep confirmed that Paul was "currently exploring all of her options, seeking support, and preparing to own and share her story."

March 19, 2026: Dakota Mortensen Breaks Silence on the Allegations

Mortensen spoke out about the domestic violence allegations between himself and Paul, telling E! News in a March 19 statement, "As anyone who has seen the video will understand, this is a deeply upsetting situation."

"I am, unfortunately, used to these baseless claims about me and our relationship," he said, "which I categorically deny."

"I am focusing on our son and his safety," Paul added, "and hope that Taylor will do the same."

March 20, 2026: Dakota Mortensen Granted Temporary Custody of Son

Mortensen was awarded temporary custody of their son after filing for a protective order against Paul, according to documents obtained by People March 20. A hearing in the matter was scheduled for April 7—where Taylor would be allowed to speak and share her side—but until then, the order stated that "no parent time is allowed," per the outlet.

March 24, 2026: Third Police Investigation

Authorities in Utah began investigating another alleged domestic violence incident that took place in 2024 which Mortensen brought to the police's attention in February, a West Jordan Police Department spokesperson told NBC News March 24. While investigators spoke to Paul's attorney, they had not yet spoken to her directly, and hoped for her to submit a written statement or be interviewed to corroborate details of Mortensen's report, per the spokesperson.

April 14, 2026: Salt Lake County District Attorney's Office Announced It Would Not File New Charges Against Taylor Frankie Paul

A week after Paul was granted supervised visitation with her and Mortensen's son during an April 7 court hearing, The Salt Lake County District Attorney’s Office announced in a news release it would not be filing charges against her after two separate investigations led by the Draper Police Department and West Jordan Police Department, according to the Salt Lake Tribune.

According to the outlet, the news release noted, "Due to the high profile of the defendant, the cases were reviewed by multiple attorneys."

#770. 'No racism in Spain' – De la Fuente message for Tuchel

Luis de la Fuente agreed a contract extension in September to stay as Spain boss until 2032

Luis de la Fuente has dismissed concerns over racism in Spanish football before the national team's Uefa Nations League meeting with England in Madrid on Sunday.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel had earlier confirmed he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the fixture, which will determine who finishes top of League A Group 3.

While he has stressed he didn't expect there to be any incidents, the visit will be England's first to the Spanish capital since a notorious 2004 encounter at the Bernabeu was overshadowed by racist chanting directed at their players.

Spain head coach De la Fuente was asked whether Tuchel's message to his players showed there was still work needed to tackle racism in Spain.

But he responded: "What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism.

"Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us."

The Spanish Football Federation was fined last month and ordered to partially close a stadium after supporters directed Islamophobic and xenophobic chants towards Muslims during a match against Egypt in Barcelona.

In the domestic game, Real Madrid's Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr has been a vocal anti-racism campaigner after frequently being on the end of racist chanting - and worse. In 2024 three Valencia fans were sentenced to eight months in prison for abusing him at a match.

Uefa operates a three-step protocol, allowing referees to stop matches, take players off the pitch temporarily and, ultimately, abandon a game if discriminatory behaviour continues.

Tuchel said on Friday: "Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid]. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch."

However, when asked again about his views at a pre-match news conference on Saturday, Tuchel added: "I never talk about racism in Spain.

"I answered politely a question about what happens, I never expect racism. I got asked, 'what will happen if and if and if?'. And I said, 'if it happens, there's a protocol in place'. That's it.

"But my trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: brings people together and not divide people."

Midfielder Declan Rice said: "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro and Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place that we followed - we came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

"The times we are in now, 2026, there should never be racism in football. It's shocking we still have it in the game today.

"I don't want to think about if one of our players or their players is racially abused because that would be a horrible mark on football."

Focusing on the match itself, De la Fuente believed both teams are currently at the pinnacle of world football, although he rejected the suggestion one could simply replicate the other's playing style.

Spain were crowned World Cup winners in the summer, while England finished third after losing to Argentina in the semi-finals.

"I prefer the Spanish model. It's very recognisable, the players are perfectly adapted," said De la Fuente. "The English model is very good, but you have to have that type of player. Neither England can play like Spain, nor Spain like England."

He suggested Spain had faced increasingly aggressive opposition as their recent success had raised expectations.

"It's our best moment in a long time," added De la Fuente, whose side also lifted the Euro 2024 title by beating England. "They are all much more aggressive to beat us now than in other times."

He also defended the value of Spanish players, arguing their performances often outweighed their transfer-market prices compared with those in the Premier League.

"Spanish footballers surprise me that, compared to what is paid in England, they are very cheap," he explained. "I see them as better, in my opinion. Everyone in their market can set the prices."

On the fitness of forward Lamine Yamal, he remained cautious over whether the Barcelona teenager would start or how long he could manage.

"We will see if he is a starter, but if he comes out, it's because he's fit to play," said De la Fuente.

Spain test will reveal if Tuchel and England have learned World Cup lessons

#769. Sam Hartman's Agent Reveals If Bachelor Will Affect Football Schedule

After Washington Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman was announced as the lead of The Bachelor season 30, his agent shared whether the ABC series would affect his time on the field.

Sam Hartman's season on The Bachelor may be quite the blitz.

After the Washington Commanders quarterback was selected as the top pick for season 30, one of his agents shared whether his search for love on the ABC series will impact his time on the field.

In fact, though the series is expected to premiere in March, the NFL star—who joined the Commanders as an undrafted free agent in 2024—shouldn't be on the end of any interceptions.

"[Filming schedule is still being worked out to accommodate the [Commanders] schedule,” Hartman's agent Brian McLaughlin told ESPN’s Kalyn Kahler Nov. 13. “He did run it by the team and they understood."

And when it came to the aspect of handing over his cell phone once filming started, McLaughlin joked that he might find a way to steal Hartman for a sec. (The show's production will overlap with the NFL free agency come March 11.)

"I plan on standing outside the mansion and yelling offers to him over the gate," he told Kahler. "I'll call the mansion landline, worst case scenario."

The glimpse into Hartman's potential shake-up comes after the 27-year-old shared his disbelief about becoming the next Bachelor lead.

"I’m excited but also very nervous," Hartman admitted on Good Morning America Nov. 13. "I have a tough time holding conversation with one girl. 30 is going to be pretty tough."

However, as Hartman joked, he likely won't need to huddle up with his squad for any words of wisdom.

“My teammates were giving me some advice on the plane ride back,” the NFL player said. “So probably not going to listen to anybody on that. But no, I'm excited.”

As for who else is thrilled, Hartman's loved ones are ready for his journey to begin as well.

“They're excited,” he said of his family. “My mom and I have a really cool relationship, and my pops is obviously just supportive. And their big thing is just be myself and enjoy the experience, and you know, trust the instincts and trust your gut.”

Until Hartman makes his rosy debut, take a look at where other Bachelor Nation couples stand today...

Lest the couple forget where their journey began, they need only walk past the master bedroom in their Dallas-area pad. That's where the graphic designer has framed the final final rose that season 17's Bachelor presented her back in that Thai forest in late 2012, right after he promised to tell her he loved her every day of the rest of their lives.

"It made sense to dry this one and make it permanent because it was accompanied by a ring and a proposal, so this is a really special thing," Catherine explained to Entertainment Tonight in 2017. Because that last rose ceremony, complete with an elephant ride and a $75,000 Neil Lane diamond, is as much part of their story as the the sweet, suburban life that followed with kids Samuel, 5, Isaiah, 3, and Mia, 2. "We don't want to shy away from the fact that we got engaged and fell in love on The Bachelor," she said, "so that is the only red rose I will allow in my house!"

The OG Bachelorette, Trista was the first to prove that a stint in the mansion could lead to love, marriage and even Bachelor babies. "Nowadays they shoot the show for, I believe, three months. So it's like 12 weeks," the author shared with Us Weekly of her 2003 season. "My show was shot in six weeks. So Ryan and I met, got engaged, got married a year later, after knowing each other for six weeks. So that's how it used to be."Their decade years holding it down as the show's success story have taught the Colorado-based pair they can handle pretty much anything. Including months sheltering in place with their kids, son Maxwell, 14, and daughter Blakesley, 13. "It's really hard for us to get a date night. I think when the kids are working, we try to take advantage of that time as much as possible," she said of scheduling around the firefighter's early bird tendencies. "But yeah, we're good. We're 16 years and this too shall pass, as they say."

Who even remembers that the sweet divorced dad originally proposed to Melissa Rycroft? Okay, probably a lot of people, as his 2009 After the Final Rose switcheroo still ranks as one of the series' most shocking moments. But if all's well that end's well, the only thing that matters is that the Seattle-based parents to daughter Riley marked 10 years of marriage this past February. "Let me apologize publicly again for putting you through the Bachelor mess that I created," Jason, also dad to teen Ty, wrote in an anniversary tribute. "With that being said... it built an incredible, unique, foundation for us to build our family—showing that we can make it through anything."

In true Bachelor fashion, native Tennesseean Peyton simply knew when she laid eyes on her future husband. Though it wasn't season 10 lead Andy Baldwin. Nearly four years after the naval officer sent her home, the Bachelor Pad alum turned up at another series-related event in 2010 and spied Chris, fresh off his showing as Ali Fedotowsky's runner-up. "It's one of those things where I've had a ton of serious relationships," she later explained to People, "and I met this kid and he was genuine, outgoing and hilarious and we just click."By the following June, the landscaper was proposing at his home in Cape Cod. And more than a decade, two kids (daughter Lyla, 5, and son Hayes, 3) and a few HGTV and DIY Network shows later, they credit the series with laying their foundation. As Peyton put it in an August 2020 Instagram post, "Without the show I'm not sure our paths would have ever crossed."

For as much as the wedding dress designer seemed to key in on Brooks Forester during her 2013 season, it was sweet mortgage lender Chris and his thoughtful prose that proved to be the perfect fit. More than seven years after their L.A. vows (during which the Desiree Hartsock Bridal designer wore two of her own original creations) they're settled in Portland, Oregon, with sons Asher, 5, and Zander, 3. "If our life were a storybook I would be the damsel in distress," the host of podcast Heart of Purpose surmised in a February 2020 post. "Chris would be the funny yet charming knight who saves the day, Asher would be the pragmatic problem solver while his little brother would be the carefree sidekick trying to kiss all the ladies!" And they would all enjoy a happy ending. As Desiree put it in a post acknowledging the choice of Clare Crawley as Bachelorette, "Reality TV worked for me!"

The gold standard in Paradise success stories, the married duo have inspired countless rose seekers to turn up in Mexico with visions of Neil Lane diamonds and Chris Harrison-officiated vows dancing in their heads. The couple's time on the spin-off's second season yielded both, and with son Reed's November 2020 arrival, they'll tie the Lowes for most Bachelor offspring. "Life gets crazy sometimes," Jade wrote in a January anniversary post of juggling 4-year-old daughter Emmy and 2-year-old son Brooks, "but I wouldn't want to go through this hand-in-hand with anyone but you. I would choose you 1000 times over."

When the Bachelor in Paradise alum returned to the beaches of Nayarit, he was initially hesitant to pursue the Bachelor finalist, worried his peripatetic lifestyle wouldn't "mesh" with the former beauty queen's. But nearly three years (plus one brief breakup and a scary December 2019 ski accident that saw Dean laid up in Switzerland for weeks) later, they, and the van he calls home, are jelling just fine. "Obviously I was wrong about that because things are going well," he shared on his podcast Help! I Suck at Dating in October 2019, months before they started wearing rings to show their shared commitment. Mostly, he appreciates that she has a healthy level of snark and the ability to handle his jokes. "I can be myself around her," he continued. "Which is a nice change."

Though he skipped the Neil Lane-sponsored proposal on Bachelor in Paradise in 2018, Kevin was ready to take a knee by the following fall, proposing in his native Toronto where he and Astrid share a home. While they've since had to push off their planned November 2020 vows in her Florida hometown, "We're actually okay with it," Astrid wrote on Instagram, noting that making the decision to postpone due to the coronavirus pandemic allowed them to focus on their connection more than the myriad wedding details. "I wouldn't want to tackle 2020 & the rest of life with anyone else by my side." Now "back in the full swing of wedding planning," as she put it on Instagram, they'll wed this October just weeks before son August's first birthday.

Even the most wishful of Bachelorette fans likely weren't betting on JoJo and Jordan's journey leading them to an altar. Because with the persistent rumors of the former Vanderbilt quarterback's ill intentions ramping up even before they took the stage for the requisite grin-and-gush After the Final Rose appearance in 2016, it seemed unlikely she would still be wearing her 3.75-carat Neil Lane diamond years later.Which, she's not. But only because Jordan presented the real estate developer with an upgrade in August 2019. Though their summer 2020 wedding plans were scrapped due to the pandemic ("I know it will be all more worth the wait," JoJo wrote in a post acknowledging their would-be June day), they tied the knot in May 2022. "You make me laugh, love me endlessly, encourage me to be brave, and always, without fail, are my biggest cheerleader," the native Texan wrote in a post on their fourth anniversary. "Can't wait for what the rest of our lives have in store for us."

Consider Ashley the poster child for ignoring all of the standard he's-just-not-that-into-you signs. Because after four years of lusting for the guy she declared her dream man upon sight, she was proven right at their August 2019 vows in Newport, R.I. Every bit as all-in as his bride, who welcomed their son Dawson in January, Jared reflected on their perfect day on Instagram, writing, "Ashley is my best friend, my person, my soulmate and now my wife. I love this woman more than words will ever allow me to express."

Who needs Neil Lane and a beach backdrop when you have this much imagination? The Dallas-based real estate agent went big when proposing to his Paradise love in May 2019. "She thought it was a normal shoot day," Adam told E! News of his plan to turn a set-up for her online boutique into an impromptu engagement session. "We were at the helicopter pad on the roof and Raven had roses in her hand. She was throwing the petals up for cute photos. She did a few practice runs and then the videographer slipped me the ring and once she threw the petals up, I got down on one knee. I blacked out, but I got everything out that I wanted."

Three months after their April 2021 vows, she announced she was expecting son Gates. "OVER THE MOON EXCITED TO SHARE THE NEWS!" she wrote on social media. "I've loved you before you were in my womb!" Raven and Adam welcomed the child in January 2022.

Sure, she waffled a bit in the early days of Paradise, unsure if her heart belonged to Barbour or Blake Horstmann, but once she zeroed in on the tech entrepreneur, she truly committed. Now the California-based duo are busying themselves with putting together their dream nuptials. While Barbour is set on a good DJ and "maybe an In-N-Out truck," Godwin is thinking big picture. "I have a few little things saved on social media," she told E! News in November 2019. "I have such fun ideas, but good weather, a cool view and a really good time. That's the one thing we do talk about and reiterate."

So he pulled a Mesnick? More than three years after Bachelor Arie dumped onetime fiancée Becca Kufrin on-air to start things up again with Lauren, the pair are married (Chris Harrison officiated their January 2019 wedding in Hawaii, natch), loving life with their 2-year-old daughter Alessi and 11-month-old twins Lux and Senna and perfecting the art of getting through tough times together. Following a heartbreaking 2020 miscarriage, Arie gifted his bride with an eternity band symbolizing "that we will always have each other in our darkest times," Lauren explained. "i think it's safe to say he gets husband of the year." To hear Arie tell it, though, makes him the lucky one. "The fact is, I'm really happy with Lauren," he told GQ in 2018 of their origin story. "So for me, it was all worth it."

#768. Simple Plan, Hoobastank & More Take Warped Tour Mid-Flight Amid FAA Ground Stop

The Used and LØLØ also joined Southwest's Live at 35 concert series aboard a flight to Orlando, Fla.

Several artists from this year’s Vans Warped Tour lineup gave passengers an unexpected in-flight concert en route to Orlando, Florida.

On Friday (Nov. 13), Simple Plan, Hoobastank, The Used and LØLØ performed aboard a Southwest Airlines flight from Los Angeles to Orlando as an FAA ground stop halted departures across the country. The musicians were headed to the city for Warped Tour’s Saturday (Nov. 14) date at Camping World Stadium.

Videos shared by passengers captured Hoobastank frontman Doug Robb performing an acoustic version of the band’s hit “The Reason,” which peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2004.

“I’ve always said @hoobastank is one of the best live acts on the planet,” one person wrote over a clip on Instagram. “This is what they sound like over airplane speakers. Insane!”

Simple Plan frontman Pierre Bouvier also performed acoustic versions of “Perfect” and “I’m Just a Kid.” And The Used played “The Taste of Ink,” while LØLØ performed her track “hot girls in hell.”

Southwest shared several clips from the performance on its Instagram Stories. The concert was part of the airline’s Live at 35 series, which brings surprise live musical performances to passengers at a cruising altitude of approximately 35,000 feet.

“Group therapy but it’s just singing perfect with Simple Plan on a plane,” another person wrote over a video of the band’s performance on Instagram, adding the caption, “Live at 35 is the best kind of therapy.”

An influencer’s video also showed some of the activities passengers enjoyed before boarding, including airport photo opportunities, karaoke and meet-and-greets at the gate. Warped Tour-branded goodie bags were waiting on passengers’ seats before the surprise performances began.

Since launching in 2011, Southwest’s Live at 35 series has featured notable acts including Imagine Dragons, Barenaked Ladies, Plain White T’s, NEEDTOBREATHE, O.A.R. and Better Than Ezra.

The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop Friday, grounding flights for more than four hours and contributing to more than 12,500 cancellations across Friday and Saturday. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed the disruption to outdated air traffic control technology and overloaded equipment, according to ABC News.

Vans Warped Tour Orlando is scheduled for Saturday, with performances by Simple Plan, Sublime, Third Eye Blind, 311, Hoobastank and others. Sunday’s lineup includes Jimmy Eat World, Taking Back Sunday, New Found Glory, The Used and Motion City Soundtrack.

On Saturday morning, Warped Tour founder Kevin Lyman shared a video on Instagram discussing how the FAA ground stop could impact the festival weekend.

“We will have a few bands canceling and we will be updating you on that,” Lyman said. “Not as many as we thought, because the bands are working hard to change their flights. Some bands have jumped in vans and [are] driving from as far away as Chicago and Houston.

He continued, “We’re going to push some bands that were playing today, [they] will be playing on Sunday. We’ve extended the sets out and giving bands more time to play. Bear with us. We’re all working hard.”

#767. Simple Plan, Hoobastank Give Surprise Flight Performance Amid FAA Stop

Simple Plan, Hoobastank and more artists headed for the Warped Tour surprised passengers with a mid-flight performance as flights were grounded due to the nationwide ground stop.

Life can be a nightmare and not fair, but Simple Plan, Hoobastank and The Used made sure travelers weren’t alone and were having fun on a flight.

That’s why the rock bands surprised people on a Southwest flight from Los Angeles to Florida with impromptu performances amid the nationwide ground stop on Nov. 13.

While the groups were on their way to Orlando for Vans Warped Tour 2026, they made 35,000 feet in the air their stage, with the bands performing a handful of their respective greatest hits, according to social footage shared by passengers, along with videos posted on the Warped Tour’s official Instagram account.

And though the reason for the FAA’s ground stop is still up in the air, Hoobastank’s lead singer Doug Robb and guitarist Dan Estrin found a way to show a side of the band fans didn’t know, performing their hits “The Reason” and “Crawling in the Dark,” per social videos.

As singer Lolo—who was also en route to Warped Tour and performed in the air—wrote alongside footage of Hoobastank’s surprise performance on Instagram, “Every plane was grounded today, but the emo gods made sure this one flew.”

Meanwhile, for Simple Plan’s mid-flight gig, lead singer Pierre Bouvier took up the mic and his guitar, warming millennials' hearts everywhere as he sang several of the punk band’s hits, such as the songs from their 2002 debut album, “I’m Just a Kid” and “Perfect,” along with the 2004 track “Welcome to Life,” according to footage shared by Warped Tour and passengers.

As for The Used’s performance, vocalist Bert McCraken and guitarist Joey Bradford took passengers—who sang along—on a trip down memory lane, performing the rock band’s songs “All That I’ve Got” and “The Taste of Ink,” per social videos, including from one traveler, who praised the “in-flight entertainment.”

And though the flight was later revealed to be a part of Southwest’s “Live at 35” surprise plane concert series, the bands were grateful to bring joy to passengers on the plane, which Robb told Rocksound Nov. 14 was “one of the last” to depart before the shutdown.

“[It] was just an extremely awesome and hilarious coincidence,” he added, “because we're on the plane going, ‘Are we okay? Is everything okay?’ But everything seems fine, so let's start singing.”

And the love was felt throughout the flight. As Robb put it, “It felt like a tube full of happy people.”

For a perfect look at the best bands of all time, keep reading…

Backstreet's back, alright! The Backstreet Boys released their first album in 1996, and redefined the turn of the century with 1999 record Millennium. Thankfully, Nick Carter, Howie Dorough, AJ McLean, Brian Littrell and Kevin Richardson are still touring and belting our favorite hits over two decades later.

All hail the girl group that gave us Beyoncé! Don't "Bug a Boo" when it comes to Destiny's Child because Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams are still icons in their own right to this day as well.

Justin Timberlake, Joey Fatone, Lance Bass, JC Chasez and Chris Kirkpatrick made up the iconic boy band group, 'NSYNC. We're still holding out for another reunion performance, and we promise, no strings attached because we aren't ready to say "Bye, Bye, Bye" just yet.

If you wanna be their lover, you've gotta get with their friends...and they sure have a lot! The Spice Girls rocked the U.K. with their '90s fashion and catchy lyrics. Mel C, Victoria Beckham, Mel B, Geri Halliwell and Emma Bunton were the Brit girl group of our dreams.

Far out, man. The Hanson brothers joined the ranks of fellow '90s boy bands with hit song, "MMMBop." Hanson released an album together in 2013 before brothers Isaac Hanson, Taylor Hanson and Zac Hanson went their separate ways for solo careers—and in Taylor's case, raising seven kids! Thankfully, our favorite bros reunited in 2018 for album String Theory and have continued touring since then.

Tionne "T-Boz" Watkins and Rozanda "Chilli" Thomas still make up '90s rap group TLC, after original member Lisa "Left Eye" Lopes tragically died in 2002. Lil Mama performed with TLC in 2013, before the "Waterfalls" singers announced their new album in 2017.

Since 2017, Korean boy band BTS has been writing, producing and performing most of their songs as international superstars. The K-pop groups loyal Army of fans are some of the most passionate in music history.

For nearly four years, Keavy Lynch, Edele Lynch, Sinéad O’Carroll, and Lindsay Armaou were all over the airwaves with 1998 breakout hits like "C'est La Vie" and "Blame it on the Weatherman"—songs featured in everything from Smart House to Dawson's Creek.  But in 2002, they parted ways after two albums... that is until reforming for 2013's The Big Reunion. And reunite they did as they've continued touring and even releasing new music, like EP Ripped Jeans in 2024.

Yep, Nick Lachey was in a boy band and we're burning up way past 98 Degrees just thinking about it. Joined by Drew Lachey and Justin Jeffre, music producers Lachey and Jeff Timmons formed the group after leaving college to pursue music careers in the '90s.

New Kids On the Block skyrocketed to fame in the late 1980s and the group reunited in 2011 for a throwback tour with The Backstreet Boys.

Original NKOTB members were brothers Jordan and Jonathan Knight, Joey McIntyre, Donnie Wahlberg and Danny Wood. The group broke up in 1994 but then reunited several years later and went on tour with the Backstreet Boys in 2011. Not surprisingly, that tour announcement pretty much broke the Internet. They are still performing today.

Thank god the JoBros are back! The Jonas Brothers gave us Nick Jonas' sweet smile, Joe Jonas' swagger and Kevin Jonas' big brother charisma. Oh, did we mention they can all sing and play instruments too? Excuse us while we're still swooning over these A-listers since their band debuted in 2006.

One of the best bands to ever come out of a singing competition series, One Direction took over the planet in the 2010s. And, the boy band has birthed plenty of successful solo careers, with Zayn Malik, Louis Tomlinson, Niall Horan, Harry Styles and the late Liam Payne all solidifying their place in music (and fashion and film) history.

The X Factor-formed group are princesses of pop and sing about body positivity, feminism, the pressures of social media and juggling it all as young moms.

Lisa, Rosé, Jennie and Jisoo make up K-pop group BLACKPINK, who released their first album—aptly titled, THE ALBUM—in October 2020. "BLACKPINK is—we kind of felt like there's two colors that represented us the most ‘cause we're very girly but at the same time we're very savage too," Rosé explained on Jimmy Kimmel Live at the time. "We have a song called ‘Pretty Savage' and it kind of goes with ‘black pink' and so we thought it described us the best."

Before the world experienced "Work From Home" life due to the coronavirus pandemic, Fifth Harmony gave fans an upbeat (and sexy) anthem to any WFH woes. Breakout singer Camila Cabello went on to have a successful solo career—including even playing Cinderella!—after the girl group went on hiatus in 2018 and other members have also released solo projects.

Australian rockers 5 Seconds of Summer first started on YouTube before singles "She Looks So Perfect" and "Girls Talk Boys" got radio play. Eventually 5SOS opened on tour for One Direction, and the rest is history.

Still performing as a trio, Boyz II Men's Nathan Morris, Shawn Stockman and Wanya Morris have been rocking the charts with hits like "I'll Make Love to You" and "One Sweet Day" for over 30 years.

The bad boy counterpart to One Direction, U.K.-based The Wanted hit it big stateside with 2012 banger "Glad You Came," before starring in their own E! reality series, The Wanted Life. The group went on hiatus in 2014 before reuniting in 2021, but sadly, founding member Tom Parker died of brain cancer the following year.

CNCO formed in 2016 with members Joel Pimentel, Richard Camacho, Erick Brian Colón, Christopher Vélez and Zabdiel De Jesús but gave their last performance as a five-some on May 14 after Pimental announced he was exiting the group.

From Nickelodeon to national tours, Big Time Rush rocked hard for five years before parting ways in 2014. Good thing all four members—Kendall Schmidt, Logan Henderson, Carlos PenaVega and James Maslow—reunited for two new shows in Dec. 2021.

British pop group Girls Aloud made history as one of the first bands formed from a reality competition series. The year was 2002, the show was Popstars: The Rivals and the powerhouse vocalists were Sarah Harding, Cheryl (then known as Cheryl Cole), Nadine Coyle, Nicola Roberts and Kimberley Walsh. Girls Aloud recorded 20 consecutive top 10 singles and four number ones, including "Sound of the Underground," during their reign.

Liftoff is scheduled for 5:45 p.m. ET today (Nov. 13).

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Update for 6:25 p.m. ET: SpaceX has launched the Starship Flight 15 mission, but did skip the first stage Super Heavy booster landing. See launch video and our full Starship Flight 15 liftoff wrap.

SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live.

Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before.

You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan.

Starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as Super Heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called Starship, or Ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight.

The rapidity of Starship's reuse hinges heavily on SpaceX's recovery strategy: Returning both vehicles directly to the launch mount will enable much faster inspection, refurbishment and reflight, the company has said.

SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy, pulling the feat off on three previous Starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover.

So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX.

"If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company wrote in a Flight 15 mission description.

The action will unspool over two days, if all goes to plan. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6.5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit.

The upper stage will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28.

Ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22.5 hours after liftoff.

There's no guarantee things will go according to plan, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any issues during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile.

So it'll be a busy weekend for SpaceX, and for space fans who want to keep tabs on the mission. And we can help you out there, with our Flight 15 updates page.

#765. SLAC scientists find conclusive proof of a mysterious third type of magnetism

For nearly 90 years, physicists have divided magnetic materials into two main categories: ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Now, scientists have confirmed that a third type exists, revealing a previously unrecognized form of magnetic behavior that could lead to major advances in computing and electronics.

The breakthrough comes from a research team led by the U.S. Department of Energy's SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory. In a study published in Science, the researchers presented compelling experimental evidence for altermagnetism, a distinct magnetic phase that combines important characteristics of the two traditionally recognized types.

"In the past few years, scientists have observed phenomena that don't fit neatly into the ferromagnetism-antiferromagnetism dichotomy," explained lead author Daniel Jost, associate scientist at SLAC and Stanford Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences. "Researchers have been compiling evidence of a third type of magnetism that bridges the qualities of these two classes. We believe our results provide robust experimental confirmation that this third phase -- altermagnetism -- is real."

The team focused on manganese telluride (MnTe), a material that had long been classified as an antiferromagnet. Building on earlier research, the scientists identified direct evidence of chirality, a distinctive asymmetry in the material's magnetic structure. This property resembles the way a spiral staircase or screw twists in a particular direction and provides a crucial signature of altermagnetism.

Beyond its importance for fundamental physics, the finding could help researchers develop magnetic materials with properties suited to future technologies, including advanced memory systems, quantum devices, and more energy-efficient data centers.

Understanding the Two Traditional Types of Magnetism

Magnetism is familiar from everyday experiences, whether it is a refrigerator magnet holding up a photograph or a compass aligning with Earth's magnetic field. But the physics behind these effects is far more complicated than it appears.

At the atomic level, magnetism is connected to a quantum property of electrons known as spin. Although spin is not literally an electron rotating like a tiny ball, it behaves in certain ways as though the electron has its own angular momentum. Scientists commonly describe the two possible spin orientations as "up" and "down."

When these spins become organized into particular patterns, a material can exhibit magnetic properties. However, that does not necessarily mean it will produce an externally detectable magnetic field.

In ferromagnetic materials, electron spins align in the same direction (up-up-up or down-down-down). Their combined effect produces the familiar magnetic field associated with ordinary magnets. People have used materials with this behavior for thousands of years.

A second category, identified in 1933, works differently. In antiferromagnets, neighboring electron spins point in opposite directions (up-down-up-down). Because the magnetic contributions oppose one another, they cancel out, leaving no overall magnetization.

A Third Type of Magnetism Challenges the Old Rules

For almost nine decades, these two categories provided the basic framework for understanding how magnetic order arises in materials. However, experimental observations in recent years began revealing behavior that neither category could fully explain.

Some materials displayed alternating electron spins and no overall magnetization, just like antiferromagnets. Yet they could also support useful spin currents, a property associated with ferromagnetic behavior. Spin currents allow information to be carried through the spin properties of electrons rather than relying entirely on their electrical charge.

The unusual combination suggested that scientists were dealing with something fundamentally different. In 2022, researchers introduced the term "altermagnets" for materials belonging to this proposed third magnetic class.

The key difference lies in the arrangement of atoms within the material. Altermagnets have alternating spin orientations (up-down-up-down), but the crystal structures surrounding the oppositely aligned spins are rotated relative to one another.

This rotation breaks a form of symmetry that exists in conventional antiferromagnets. Although the distinction is subtle, it can dramatically change how electrons behave, allowing altermagnets to combine properties once considered incompatible.

Scientists Find the Missing Evidence for Altermagnetism

Even as experimental support for altermagnetism accumulated, researchers still needed a decisive way to establish that it represented a genuinely distinct magnetic phase.

"By 2024, there were some factors that spoke strongly in favor of altermagnetism being real," Jost said, "but there was still a missing piece to the puzzle."

That missing evidence involved chirality, a property sometimes described as "handedness." An object is chiral when its mirror image cannot be perfectly aligned with the original. Human hands provide a simple example: Your left and right hands are mirror images, but a left hand cannot fit properly into a right-handed glove.

In an altermagnet, the unusual arrangement of atoms and electron spins can create this kind of handedness in the material's electronic and magnetic structure. Conventional antiferromagnets do not exhibit the same characteristic chiral signature.

Detecting that difference would provide a powerful way to distinguish a true altermagnet from a material that merely resembles one.

The researchers selected manganese telluride as their test material. For decades, scientists considered it an ordinary antiferromagnet, but more recent studies had raised the possibility that it belonged to the newly proposed category.

Powerful X-Rays Reveal a Hidden Magnetic Signature

To investigate the material's unusual properties, the team conducted experiments at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF) in France. The facility's ID32 beamline produces precisely controlled polarized X-rays, allowing scientists to examine subtle magnetic structures that are otherwise extremely difficult to detect.

The researchers used circularly polarized X-rays, which have electric fields that rotate in either a left-handed or right-handed direction as the light travels. By measuring how the material scattered these two forms of light, they could search for evidence of chirality.

"Chiral materials scatter left-handed polarized X-ray beams differently than they do right-handed beams," explained Jost. "Non-chiral materials would scatter each beam of light the same way."

The experiment revealed a clear difference in the way manganese telluride interacted with the two X-ray polarizations. This distinctive chiral response was precisely the kind of signal expected from altermagnetism and would not be present in a conventional antiferromagnet.

"This chiral signature gave us the solid experimental ground to say altermagnetism stands in a class of its own," Jost said.

The researchers first performed the experiment in 2024. They returned in early 2025 and repeated the measurements, successfully reproducing the results and strengthening the evidence for the new magnetic phase.

"This technique helped us confirm that manganese telluride was really exhibiting altermagnetic properties," said Rachel Nickel, postdoctoral scientist with ESRF, a co-author who helped design and conduct the experiment on the ID32 beamline. "Altermagnetism was only proposed a few years ago, and the rapid progress in confirming these models is incredible."

Why Altermagnetism Could Transform Future Computers

The discovery could have important consequences for spintronics, a growing field that seeks to use electron spin to develop more capable electronic devices.

Conventional electronics store and process information primarily by controlling the electrical charge of electrons. Spintronics adds another way to work with information by taking advantage of electron spin as well.

This extra capability could enable devices that operate faster, withstand interference more effectively, and consume substantially less electricity. Such improvements would be especially valuable in computer memory, large data centers, and other technologies that require enormous amounts of information processing.

However, the two traditional types of magnetism present different obstacles that have limited the development of spintronic systems.

"Ferromagnets are too easily influenced by magnetic fields," Jost explained. "If you have a permanent magnet in your pocket and walk by a spintronic device built with ferromagnets, you could start flipping the bits, scrambling the information stored there. Antiferromagnets fix that problem, but they are practically invisible -- so you can't easily read the data stored in them or use them to drive efficient spin currents."

Altermagnets offer a potentially valuable alternative. Like antiferromagnets, their opposing spins produce no overall magnetization, helping protect them against unwanted magnetic interference. At the same time, their unusual electronic structure allows them to generate spin-polarized currents that can be used to retrieve information.

"Altermagnets combine the best of both," Jost said. "They have zero net magnetization, so they're stable, but they still have the capability to generate spin-polarized currents needed to easily extract information. That gives you an additional degree of freedom to work with."

A New Frontier for Quantum Technology and Electronics

Confirming altermagnetism gives scientists a new class of materials to investigate and potentially engineer for technological applications. By combining magnetic stability with the ability to manipulate spin-based information, these materials could help overcome challenges that have held back conventional spintronic devices.

The next step will be learning how to control altermagnetic states using external influences such as light and electricity. Researchers hope that mastering this control will make it possible to design practical devices that take advantage of the unusual magnetic properties.

Although significant development is still needed before these materials can be widely used, the findings establish a stronger experimental foundation for future work on quantum technologies, computer memory, and more efficient data centers.

The research received partial funding from the DOE Office of Science.

#764. Karol G Surprises Mexico City Fans With Thalía as Special Guest: ‘The First Person I Wanted to Be’

The Nov. 13 show at the GNP Seguros Stadiums marked the first performance of the Mexican pop icon in Mexico City.

Karol G gave her fans a huge surprise on Friday (Nov. 13) during the first of her three nights at the Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City, inviting Thalia to join her on stage for a special performance. The appearance of the iconic Mexican pop star, who had not performed in the capital for a decade, sent the audience into a frenzy. Explore Karol G Thalia See latest videos, charts and news

“She was my first idol in life,” an emotional Karol G told the 65,000 concertgoers during her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, according to promoter Ocesa. “The first person I wanted to be, when I dreamed of becoming a singer, was named Thalia, and she’s here with me tonight.” Related Simple Plan, Hoobastank & More Take Warped Tour Mid-Flight Amid FAA Ground Stop Journey Drummer Deen Castronovo Exits Mid-Tour to Focus on His Health John Summit, David Guetta, Alison Wonderland & More to Play College Football Playoff National Championship Weekend

Before Thalia appeared, a video was shown of a young Karol G saying that she wanted to be like her. The Mexican superstar then took to the stage wearing a replica of her iconic guitar-shaped bustier from her “Amor a la Mexicana” era — one of the most famous outfits in Latin pop culture. The new version of the outfit was decorated by Thalia herself, as she had teased a few days earlier in an Instagram post without revealing its purpose.

Together, they performed Thalia’s classics “Piel Morena” and “Amor a la Mexicana,” followed by “¿A Quién le Importa?” — a cover of the Spanish group Alaska y Dinarama’s hit, which Thalia reimagined in 2002.

The singer and actress known for telenovelas like María la del Barrio and Marimar praised Karol G’s strength and resilience. “She doesn’t care what the world has to say about her,” Thalia said while singing the Alaska y Dinarama anthem, getting a roaring cheer from the audience as they celebrated the union of two stars from different generations.

During her first of three nights in Mexico City, Karol G emphasized how meaningful Thalia’s presence was, especially since it marked the first time in 10 years that the Mexican icon had stepped onto a stage in the capital city.

“Only you, as a Latina, carry this light everywhere,” Thalia said in response to the Colombian superstar’s praises. Karol, visibly moved, even shed a few tears. “This Mexico adores you! We love and cherish you,” Thalia added.

Karol — who just won the day before two Latin Grammys (best urban music album for Tropicoqueta and best reggaeton performance for “Verano Rosa” with Feid) — has brought several artists out of retirement or long hiatuses to perform alongside her. In 2022, she invited Mexican singer Anahí to sing RBD’s hit “Sálvame” as a duet at the Arena Ciudad de México. In 2024, she brought Spanish singer Amaia Montero to the stage at Madrid’s Santiago Bernabéu Stadium to perform “Rosas” from La Oreja de Van Gogh.

By the time Thalia made her appearance on Friday, the crowd was already electrified, especially after Karol G performed her hit “Ese Hombre Es Malo” with her all-female mariachi band. Earlier, she had also donned a white top and a skirt in the colors of the Mexican flag — green, white and red — along with a dramatic feathered headdress during her performance of “Tropicoqueta.”

Another highlight of the night came with the song “¿Con Quién Andará?,” a track from No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, which she has described as her favorite on the album. The song was performed live for the first time during her Nov. 4th celebration party streamed on TikTok.

Karol G’s next shows at the Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City are set for Saturday and Sunday (Nov. 14 and 15) as part of the kickoff for the Latin American leg of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour. Days earlier, she performed three shows in the northern Mexican city of Monterrey, on Nov. 6, 7 and 8, at the Estadio BBVA. In both cities, Mexican-American star Becky G opened the shows, performing songs like “Marathon,” “Patrona,” “Chula” and “2 AM.”

#763. ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Soundtrack: See the Full 34-Song Tracklist

The album arrives Nov. 19 alongside the long-awaited video game.

With Grand Theft Auto VI just days away from its release, fans are getting their first look at the long-awaited video game’s all-star soundtrack.

Photos and videos of the vinyl edition of Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album have surfaced on social media in recent days, revealing its full 34-song tracklist across two records. Sources close to the project have confirmed the tracklist to Billboard.

The collection features a genre-spanning lineup of artists, including Playboi Carti, Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Lana Del Rey, Gunna, Yung Lean, Future, Metro Boomin, Travis Scott, Fred again.., PinkPantheress, Morgan Wallen, Tame Impala, Fuerza Regida and more. Several of the songs are already available on streaming services.

Announced in September by Atlantic Records and Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album is set to arrive Nov. 19, the same day the game launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

The album’s music is designed to capture the energy and atmosphere of Vice City and Leonida, the fictional locations featured in the game. It also continues the Grand Theft Auto franchise’s long-standing tradition of introducing players to new music and emerging musical subcultures.

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album will be available through several retailers, including Blood Records, Best Buy, Walmart, Amazon, Barnes & Noble, Target and Urban Outfitters, as well as independent record stores. Each retailer will offer an exclusive vinyl pressing featuring its own unique design and poster.

In addition to the soundtrack, the game will feature several radio stations hosted and curated by artists including Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Morgan Wallen, Trina and Trick Daddy, Burna Boy and Robyn.

Beyond the album, Grand Theft Auto VI will be celebrated with a music festival at Miami’s Mana Wynwood on Nov. 21. SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov. 13): Don't panic.

The company's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms.

On Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. The company shared photos of the move on X, and in two of those shots we can see some intriguing words inked on the spacecraft: "Don't panic."

The phrase is familiar to fans of Douglas Adams' sci-fi classic "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy": In the novel, the electronic guidebook that helps travelers find their way across the cosmos has "Don't panic!" on its cover.

And Ship 42 itself is connected to the beloved book, by virtue of its serial number. In "The Hitchhiker's Guide," a supercomputer named Deep Mind is asked to come up with "the answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything." It thinks for 7.5 million years and comes up with "42."

SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk has voiced his affection for "The Hitchhiker's Guide" in the past — and he has already paid tribute to it with a well-placed "Don't panic."

The debut launch of SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket back in February 2018 sent Musk's red Tesla Roadster into orbit around the sun, with a spacesuit-clad mannequin named Starman at the wheel and its entertainment display programmed to read "Don't panic!"

Starship Flight 15 is scheduled to launch today during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). You can watch it here at Space.com.

If all goes according to plan, Starship's Super Heavy first stage will come back to Starbase for a chopsticks catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff.

Ship 42, meanwhile, will head to orbit, a destination that Starship reached for the first time on Flight 14, which took place on Sept. 28. Ship 42 will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites today — the second batch of the spacecraft to reach orbit. (The first set of 26 were delivered on Flight 14).

Ship 42 will stay up for a while after that, circling Earth 14 times before coming back for its own chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after launch.

That's the plan, anyway; SpaceX will only go through with a Ship catch attempt if all systems on the vehicle look good. If there are any problems, the company will divert to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, near either Hawaii or Chile.

Both of Starship's stages — Super Heavy and the Ship — are designed to be rapidly reusable. And "rapidly" is a bit of understatement: SpaceX wants to launch 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030, Musk has said.

The chopsticks-catch strategy is a big part of that vision. Bringing both Starship stages directly back to the launch mount will greatly reduce the time needed for inspection, refurbishment and reflight, according to SpaceX.

The company has already caught Super Heavy on three previous Starship test flights. It has never tried to do so with Ship, instead targeting ocean splashdowns with the upper stage.

The double catch attempt may be unprecedented, but SpaceX seems to be taking its own advice: There's no panic around Flight 15 or its bold goals.

"I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," Musk said last month, during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz. To find out what his latest project is, you can follow Michael on Twitter.
